title: Transfer fibre gradients to gamma-count energy without a dimension sum
statement: Let mu(dx)=Z^-1 exp(sigma.x)Dir_alpha(dx), pi(n)=Z^-1 prod_i[(alpha_i) rising(n_i) sigma_i^n_i/n_i!]/[(alpha0) rising(|n|)], and nu(n,dx)=pi(n)Dir_(alpha+n)(dx). Givenx, n_i are independent Pois(sigma_i x_i), so total count is dominated byPois(S), all moments finite; sigma_i=0 forces n_i=0 on support. The reversible count chain has birthsigma_i(alpha_i+n_i)/2,deathn_i(alpha0+|n|-1)/2, detailed balance and linear-birth nonexplosion. For b=alpha+n,b0=sum b,F(n)=Dir_b f and A=diag x-xx^T, Dirichlet integration by parts gives F(n+e_i)-F(n)=Dir_b[(A grad f)_i]/b_i. Ifu=Dir_b[A grad f],Q=Dir_b[grad f^T A grad f]=2E_b(f), then Dir_b A=[diag b-bb^T/b0]/(b0+1). Vector Cauchy-Schwarz and the positive rank-one subtraction give sum_i(sigma_i/b_i)u_i^2<=2S E_b(f)/(b0+1), hence E_D(F)<=S E_mu(f)/(alpha0+1), where E_mu=1/2 mu[grad f^T A grad f] and E_D=sum_n pi(n)sum_i sigma_i(alpha_i+n_i)[Delta_i F]^2/2. This uses max fitnessS rather than sum sigma_i and assumes no log-concavity. It is a mathematical joint law/energy comparison, not a supplied sampler or actual count gap.
